review.brief: Review the FULL diff of this change on ft/RM30-MAG-30-supercharger-stats-read-from-charging (commits 2656a9b, 7cf0eb2, 7d4e80f, 2febed7) against its artifacts. Validate: (1) MODULE BOUNDARY — nothing outside internal/gateway/ except the granted ai/architecture.md, README.md and the leader's cmd/web/main.go integration; gateway reaches charging ONLY through charging.SessionReader, never chargingdb; the two analytics-owned telemetry.NewSuperchargerReader calls in cmd/web/main.go are correctly untouched (roadmap D2). (2) ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — /supercharger-stats now reads charge_sessions via the charging module (MAG-30 AC1); gateway no longer reads telemetry for this path (AC2); docs updated (AC3). (3) DESIGN COMPLIANCE — every design.md decision D1-D10, especially D3 (single reverse), D4 (CountryCode/BillingType gone everywhere), D9a (plain UTC today, no browserToday) and D9b (end.After(today) -> 400, end == today accepted). (4) TEST-CONTRACT FIDELITY — supercharger_test.go must assert the T1-T14 expectations design.md authored BEFORE implementation, not whatever the code happens to do. Check specifically that T14's ~180-day window means the 400-day cap cannot be what rejects it, and that fakeSessionReader keeps the D8 TeslaID-nil exclusion. Judge tests by READING them; do not run them. (5) PERFORMANCE-PROFILE — one bounded read per render, no N+1, no unbounded scan. (6) LEADER EDITS — four leader interventions are in the diff and get the same scrutiny as worker code, not a pass: D5 (superchargerStatsViewFor helper + renderError on the Page 400 path), and D8 (the two AGENTS.md doc corrections). (7) ANTI-GAMING — no acceptance criterion weakened, no Test Contract case dropped or hollowed, no self-approved status. findings.note: internal/gateway/handlers/supercharger.go:154 — SuperchargerStatsPage's 400 path now calls renderError, which sets HX-Error-Fragment: true. design.md D1 (lines ~163-166) explicitly states 'SuperchargerStatsPage uses plain render at the same 400 status, because it is a full top-level page navigation, not an htmx swap target.' The leader's wave-2 decision D5 (progress.json decisions[]) consciously overrode this and switched Page's 400 path to renderError, reasoning that render omits the header. That reasoning is actually the stronger read of the binding project rule in ai/htmx-go-integration.md ('a non-2xx error fragment MUST be rendered with renderError ... if the non-2xx body is a component, it goes through renderError') and is functionally harmless here (the nav link to /supercharger-stats is a plain <a href>, not htmx-boosted, so the extra header is inert on a normal browser navigation — confirmed no HX-Error-Fragment/renderError assertion exists in supercharger_test.go for the Page route, and no other renderError call in the codebase targets a full-page route, so this is a genuinely new pattern). The gap is that design.md D1 was never amended to reflect this reversal — unlike D9, which got an explicit 'revised — leader triage' rewrite when the leader changed course. A future reader of design.md alone would believe the code still uses plain render on the Page path. RE-VERIFIED round 1 follow-up: leader amended design.md D1 in place with a 'REVISED at Apply (wave 2, decisions D5; confirmed by review round 1 finding R1-1)' note (design.md lines ~168-177) that keeps the original paragraph, states the actual shipped behavior (renderError, not render), and gives the corrected rationale — the binding ai/htmx-go-integration.md rule is keyed on what the response body IS (a renderable component), not on who consumes it, so a component-body 400 goes through renderError regardless of route; renderError is render plus one header, byte-identical for a plain browser GET today, and keeps the Page/Fragment entry points symmetric against a future htmx-driven navigation to this route. This fully resolves the documentation-fidelity gap the finding raised — design.md and the shipped code now agree, with the same kind of explicit revision marker D9 already used. No code, template, or test file changed; verified via re-read of design.md only, no re-run of build/vet/guards was needed since nothing they cover changed.
